ORACLE-ARITHMETIC CORRECTION (evidence-builder, from script source debate_logs/state_points_batch_concurrent_010.py): P1 t4 wrote ids base=(4+1)*1000+j = 5000..5004 and P1 t5 wrote 6000..6004; P2's id 5000 and P3's shared ids 6001..6004 were therefore PRE-EXISTING. Correct expectations: P2 count = 50 (id 5000 overwritten, doc: 'points with the same id will be overwritten when re-uploaded'), P3 count = 46 non-shared + 8 shared visible = 54. Observed 50 and 54 EXACTLY match; the script's 51 and 59 double-count the 5 colliding ids (59-54 = 5 = |{5000,6001,6002,6003,6004}|).

COMPARATIVE OBSERVATION (count face vs batch-get face, same final state, rest): count(P3 exact)=54 equals 46 non-shared + 8 shared returned by batch-get — the two read faces AGREE; the log's 'read-face disagreement' is an artifact of the script's expected-value arithmetic, not of the server. The collections+get points_count third face was not called by the script (face_unavailable).

P1 control leg behaved correctly: all 10 concurrent disjoint single-op batches returned 200 with per-op results ('[P1 count] status=200 raw={"result":{"count":50}...' -> '[P1] OK: count == 50'); all P2/P3 race requests returned 200 (no 4xx/5xx, no transport failure, wait=true on every batch).

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: batch operations are applied sequentially in the order given; each operation reports its own result
contract_grounding.note: violates=false, genuinely compliant, for two independent reasons. (1) The raw responses satisfy the assertion and the corrected arithmetic: every batch returned a per-operation result in order ('{"operation_id":N,"status":"completed"}'), and the count-face values (50/50/54) equal the corrected expectations once the script's 5 id collisions are accounted for (see secondary_observations); the documentation's own Idempotence prose ('points with the same id will be overwritten when re-uploaded') confirms re-upserting existing ids must not increase the count, so P2's observed 50 is the documented-correct value. (2) Domain note: the phenomenon the script actually attacked (cross-batch concurrency and count/get read-face agreement) lies OUTSIDE this assertion's constraint domain — each batch contained exactly ONE operation, so in-batch sequential ordering was never exercised. No contract constraint anchors cross-batch read-face agreement (closest: qdrant_behavioral_points_count_001 'exact=true returns the exact number of points matching' — count 54 with 54 live points complies; qdrant_bc_delete_points_invisibility_001 'deleted points are no longer returned by reads' — final state has all 8 shared points live after the last upserts, complies). Constraint-id recovery note: candidates.jsonl carried constraint_id="" (empty); recovered from the script header 'constraint_ids: qdrant_state_points_batch_001' and confirmed present in structured_contract.json state_constraints.

script: requests are valid single-op batch POSTs (wait=true) — well-formed; BUT the oracle's expected-count arithmetic collides ids: P2 'fresh' id 5000 is inside P1 t4's range [5000..5004] and P3 shared ids 6001..6004 are inside P1 t5's range [6000..6004] (script line: base = (t + 1) * 1000, 5 points per thread).

log: both DEFECT lines (62, 63) are computed FROM those wrong expectations; the raw count/get values (50/50/54 vs corrected 50/50/54) show the server's count face and batch-get face mutually consistent — the DEFECT_FOUND verdict is not supported by the raw observations.
chain_trace.break_detail: Break originates at the script layer: the oracle assumed id 5000 and ids 6001..6004 were new, but P1's own disjoint ranges ((t+1)*1000..+4) had already inserted them; expected counts 51 and 59 are arithmetically wrong (correct: 50 and 54). The log layer inherits the break (DEFECT lines quote the wrong expectations); the contract and doc links are intact. Net: DEFECT_FOUND verdict rests on a test-oracle arithmetic error, not on server behavior.
